correctness.rationale: The four graphs have explicit Seidel switching sets. Exhaustive enumeration verifies the same strongly regular parameters \(28,12,6,4\), common face vector \((f_0,f_1,f_2)=(28,210,420)\), no independent five-set, and tetrahedron counts \((105,73,65,65)\). The integral chain complex has rational \(\operatorname{rank}\partial_1=27\). Bitset elimination computes \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}\partial_2=183\), equalling the theoretical upper bound for the rational rank. Every triangular face extends to at most one tetrahedron, giving one distinct unit-pivot row per column of the third boundary; thus \(\partial_3\) is split injective integrally. Consequently, \(C_2/\operatorname{im}\partial_3\) is free and \(H_2=\ker\partial_2/\operatorname{im}\partial_3\) is its subgroup, hence free of rank \(420-183-f_3\), giving \(132,164,172,172\). No claim about torsion in integral first homology is made.

value.rationale: The four nonisomorphic graphs form the complete exceptionally cospectral \((28,12,6,4)\) strongly regular class, making their integral independence-complex homology a natural comparison invariant, rather than an arbitrary chosen sample. The theorem computes the previously unlocated integral second homology of all three Chang switchings and a split-injective structural explanation for its torsion-freeness. The values distinguish three homology types in one spectrum/parameter class. Their relationship to independent-four-set counts is disclosed, not misrepresented as a strictly stronger distinguishing graph invariant.
